summaries.label: First Reading
summaries.text: On his mountain the Lord will prepare a rich feast for all peoples. He will remove the veil over the nations, swallow up death and wipe away every tear, and his people will say, “This is our God; we have waited for him.”

summaries.label: Psalm
summaries.text: The Lord is the psalmist’s shepherd, giving pasture, water and guidance, and keeping him safe even in the valley of the shadow of death. He sets a table before his enemies, and goodness and mercy follow him all his days.

summaries.label: Second Reading
summaries.text: Paul has learned to be content both in plenty and in need, because he can do all things through Christ who strengthens him. He thanks the Philippians for sharing his affliction and promises that God will supply their every need.

summaries.label: Gospel
summaries.text: A king gives a wedding feast for his son. The invited refuse and kill his servants, so he destroys them and invites everyone, bad and good. A guest without wedding clothing is cast out: many are called, few are chosen.

unity: The feast Isaiah promised and the table of the psalm become the king’s wedding banquet for his son. The invitation is open, but it must be answered and the guest must come ready: set aside real time this week for prayer and Mass.
lead_in: At the king’s wedding feast in Matthew 22, Augustine hears the Bridegroom of the psalm and the Spouse of the Song of Songs.

excerpt.text: So then this Bridegroom, fair in beauty above the children of men, became deformed that He might make His Spouse fair to whom it is said, O you beauteous among women, of whom it is said, Who is this that comes up, whitened with the brightness of light, not the coloring of falsehood! He then who called them to the wedding, found a man who had not a wedding garment, and He said to him, Friend, how did you come in hither, not having a wedding garment? . . . You are all at the feast, have the wedding garment.
excerpt.attribution: St Augustine, Sermon 45 on the New Testament (Ben. 95), §5, in Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, series 1, vol. 6
